words.name: OTC
words.description: Over-the-counter (OTC) refers to trading conducted directly between two parties without the supervision of an exchange. Most foreign exchange trading takes place on OTC markets rather than on centralised exchanges.

words.name: foreign
words.description: Originating from or characteristic of a country other than the one being referenced. In finance the term typically qualifies currencies, transactions, or instruments tied to a country other than the domestic one.

words.name: instruments
words.description: Financial instruments are monetary contracts between parties. In foreign exchange markets, the main instruments include spot transactions, outright forwards, foreign exchange swaps, currency swaps, and options.

words.name: Euro
words.description: The euro (symbol: €; currency code: EUR) is the official currency of 21 of the 27 member states of the European Union. This group of states is officially known as the euro area, more commonly named the eurozone. The euro is divided into 100 euro cents.

words.name: Yen
words.description: The yen (symbol: ¥; currency code: JPY) is the official currency of Japan. It is the third most-traded currency in the foreign exchange market after the United States dollar and the euro, and is widely used as a reserve currency. The yen is divided into 100 sen, though sen are no longer used in everyday transactions.

words.name: Renminbi
words.description: The renminbi (symbol: ¥; currency code: CNY; abbreviation: RMB) is the official currency of the People's Republic of China. Its primary unit is the yuan. Issued by the People's Bank of China, the renminbi is one of the world's most-traded currencies and is included in the IMF's Special Drawing Rights basket.

words.name: other
words.description: A residual category used to group together items that are not individually itemised. In currency turnover statistics, 'other currencies' aggregates the trading volume of all currencies outside the top-ranked ones.

words.name: total
words.description: the whole amount or count, e.g. the total number of possible outcomes

words.name: net
words.description: A value that remains after specified deductions or adjustments. In foreign exchange turnover statistics, 'net' refers to adjustments removing double-counting between reporting dealers.

words.name: transaction
words.description: A completed agreement between a buyer and a seller to exchange goods, services, or financial instruments. In foreign exchange, a transaction typically involves the exchange of one currency for another at an agreed rate.

words.name: outright
words.description: An outright forward is a foreign exchange contract obliging two parties to exchange currencies at a specified rate on a future date beyond the spot settlement window. It differs from a swap in that it consists of a single leg rather than two.

words.name: forwards
words.description: Forward contracts are agreements to buy or sell an asset at a predetermined price on a specified future date. Currency forwards are widely used to hedge foreign exchange risk arising from future cash flows in foreign currencies.

words.name: swap
words.description: A currency swap (or FX swap) is a foreign exchange transaction that combines a spot purchase or sale of a currency with a simultaneous forward sale or purchase of the same currency. It is widely used to manage liquidity and hedge foreign exchange exposure.

words.name: option
words.description: A foreign exchange option gives the holder the right, but not the obligation, to exchange one currency for another at a specified rate on or before a specified date. Options are typically used to hedge or to speculate on currency movements.
The Gregorian calendar year 2022 (MMXXII), in which the BIS conducted its most recent Triennial Survey of foreign exchange turnover at the time this dataset was compiled.

The yen and yuan sign (¥) is a currency symbol used both for the Japanese yen and the Chinese yuan (the primary unit of the renminbi). It consists of the Latin letter Y crossed by one or two horizontal strokes.

triples.name: US dollar
triples.description: The United States dollar (symbol: $; currency code: USD) is the official currency of the United States and several other countries. It is the world's primary reserve currency and the most-traded currency on the foreign exchange market. The dollar is divided into 100 cents.

triples.name: U.S. dollar
triples.description: The United States dollar (symbol: $; currency code: USD) is the official currency of the United States and several other countries. It is the world's primary reserve currency and the most-traded currency on the foreign exchange market. The dollar is divided into 100 cents.

triples.name: Australian dollar
triples.description: The Australian dollar (symbol: $ or A$; currency code: AUD) is the official currency of the Commonwealth of Australia, including its external territories, as well as the independent Pacific states of Kiribati, Nauru, and Tuvalu. It is divided into 100 cents and was introduced in 1966, replacing the Australian pound.

triples.name: Canadian dollar
triples.description: The Canadian dollar (symbol: $ or C$; currency code: CAD) is the official currency of Canada. It is issued by the Bank of Canada and is one of the world's most-traded currencies. The Canadian dollar is divided into 100 cents and is often regarded as a commodity currency due to Canada's substantial natural-resource exports.

triples.name: Hong Kong dollar
triples.description: The Hong Kong dollar (symbol: HK$; currency code: HKD) is the official currency of Hong Kong. It is divided into 100 cents and has been pegged to the United States dollar since 1983 at a rate of approximately 7.80 HKD per USD. It is issued by three commercial note-issuing banks under the authority of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority.

triples.name: Singapore dollar
triples.description: The Singapore dollar (symbol: S$; currency code: SGD) is the official currency of Singapore. It is divided into 100 cents and is issued by the Monetary Authority of Singapore. It is interchangeable with the Brunei dollar at par under a Currency Interchangeability Agreement.

triples.name: New Zealand dollar
triples.description: The New Zealand dollar (symbol: NZ$; currency code: NZD) is the official currency of New Zealand and several Pacific island states (Cook Islands, Niue, Tokelau, Pitcairn Islands). It is divided into 100 cents and is informally known as the 'Kiwi dollar'. It is issued by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand.

triples.name: New Taiwan dollar
triples.description: The New Taiwan dollar (symbol: NT$; currency code: TWD) is the official currency of the Republic of China (Taiwan). It is divided into 100 cents and is issued by the Central Bank of the Republic of China. It replaced the old Taiwan dollar in 1949.

triples.name: Swiss franc
triples.description: The Swiss franc (symbol: Fr. or CHF; currency code: CHF) is the official currency and legal tender of Switzerland and Liechtenstein, and is also used in the Italian exclave of Campione d'Italia. Issued by the Swiss National Bank, it is widely regarded as a safe-haven currency due to Switzerland's political stability and low inflation.

triples.name: Japanese yen
triples.description: The Japanese yen (symbol: ¥; currency code: JPY) is the official currency of Japan, issued by the Bank of Japan. It is the third most-traded currency in the world after the US dollar and the euro, and serves as a major global reserve currency.

triples.name: Swedish krona
triples.description: The Swedish krona (symbol: kr; currency code: SEK) is the official currency of Sweden. It is divided into 100 öre and is issued by the Sveriges Riksbank, the central bank of Sweden. The plural form in Swedish is kronor.

triples.name: Danish krone
triples.description: The Danish krone (symbol: kr; currency code: DKK) is the official currency of Denmark, Greenland, and the Faroe Islands. It is divided into 100 øre and is issued by Danmarks Nationalbank. The krone is pegged to the euro through the European Exchange Rate Mechanism II.

triples.name: Norwegian krone
triples.description: The Norwegian krone (symbol: kr; currency code: NOK) is the official currency of Norway and its dependent territories. It is divided into 100 øre and is issued by Norges Bank, the central bank of Norway. The plural form in Norwegian is kroner.

triples.name: South Korean won
triples.description: The South Korean won (symbol: ₩; currency code: KRW) is the official currency of South Korea. It is issued by the Bank of Korea. Although a subunit called the jeon exists in theory (1/100 of a won), it is not used in everyday transactions due to its negligible value.

triples.name: Indian rupee
triples.description: The Indian rupee (symbol: ₹; currency code: INR) is the official currency of India. It is divided into 100 paise (singular: paisa) and is issued by the Reserve Bank of India. The rupee symbol ₹ was officially adopted in 2010.

triples.name: Mexican peso
triples.description: The Mexican peso (symbol: $ or MX$; currency code: MXN) is the official currency of Mexico. It is divided into 100 centavos and is issued by the Banco de México. The peso is one of the most-traded currencies in Latin America and serves as a common proxy for emerging-market sentiment.

triples.name: Chilean peso
triples.description: The Chilean peso (symbol: $ or CLP$; currency code: CLP) is the official currency of Chile. It is issued by the Central Bank of Chile. The peso is divided in theory into 100 centavos, but centavos are no longer used due to their negligible value.

triples.name: Philippine peso
triples.description: The Philippine peso (symbol: ₱; currency code: PHP) is the official currency of the Philippines. It is divided into 100 sentimos (also called centavos) and is issued by the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas. The peso symbol ₱ was officially adopted in 1967.

triples.name: Colombian peso
triples.description: The Colombian peso (symbol: $ or COL$; currency code: COP) is the official currency of Colombia. It is divided into 100 centavos and is issued by the Banco de la República. Centavos are no longer used in practice due to their negligible value.

triples.name: Argentine peso
triples.description: The Argentine peso (symbol: $ or ARG$; currency code: ARS) is the official currency of Argentina. It is divided into 100 centavos and is issued by the Central Bank of Argentina (Banco Central de la República Argentina). It is one of the most volatile major currencies, having been subject to repeated devaluations.

triples.name: South African rand
triples.description: The South African rand (symbol: R; currency code: ZAR) is the official currency of South Africa and is also legal tender in the Common Monetary Area together with the currencies of Lesotho, Namibia, and Eswatini. It is divided into 100 cents and is issued by the South African Reserve Bank.

triples.name: Brazilian real
triples.description: The Brazilian real (symbol: R$; currency code: BRL) is the official currency of Brazil. It is divided into 100 centavos and is issued by the Banco Central do Brasil. The current real was introduced in 1994 as part of the Plano Real economic stabilisation program.

triples.name: Polish złoty
triples.description: The Polish złoty (symbol: zł; currency code: PLN) is the official currency of Poland. It is divided into 100 groszy (singular: grosz) and is issued by the Narodowy Bank Polski. The word 'złoty' is the masculine form of the Polish adjective meaning 'golden'.

triples.name: Thai baht
triples.description: The Thai baht (symbol: ฿; currency code: THB) is the official currency of Thailand. It is divided into 100 satang and is issued by the Bank of Thailand. The baht traces its origins to a traditional unit of weight used for measuring silver.

triples.name: Indonesian rupiah
triples.description: The Indonesian rupiah (symbol: Rp; currency code: IDR) is the official currency of Indonesia. It is issued by Bank Indonesia, the central bank. The rupiah is one of the most heavily denominated currencies in the world, with banknotes commonly ranging up to 100,000 rupiah.

triples.name: Czech koruna
triples.description: The Czech koruna (symbol: Kč; currency code: CZK) is the official currency of the Czech Republic. It is divided into 100 haléř (singular: haléř), although hellers are no longer in circulation. It is issued by the Czech National Bank. The word 'koruna' means 'crown'.

triples.name: Turkish lira
triples.description: The Turkish lira (symbol: ₺; currency code: TRY) is the official currency of Turkey and Northern Cyprus. It is divided into 100 kuruş and is issued by the Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey. The current lira replaced the old lira in 2005 at a ratio of 1,000,000 old lira to 1 new lira.

triples.name: Hungarian forint
triples.description: The Hungarian forint (symbol: Ft; currency code: HUF) is the official currency of Hungary. It was historically divided into 100 fillér, although fillér coins are no longer in use. It is issued by the Hungarian National Bank (Magyar Nemzeti Bank).

triples.name: Saudi riyal
triples.description: The Saudi riyal (symbol: ﷼; currency code: SAR) is the official currency of Saudi Arabia. It is divided into 100 halalas and is issued by the Saudi Central Bank. The riyal has been pegged to the US dollar since 1986 at a rate of 3.75 SAR per USD.

triples.name: Malaysian ringgit
triples.description: The Malaysian ringgit (symbol: RM; currency code: MYR) is the official currency of Malaysia. It is divided into 100 sen and is issued by Bank Negara Malaysia, the country's central bank. The word 'ringgit' originally meant 'jagged' in Malay, referring to the milled edges of Spanish silver dollars used in colonial-era trade.

triples.name: Russian ruble
triples.description: The Russian ruble (symbol: ₽; currency code: RUB) is the official currency of the Russian Federation. It is divided into 100 kopecks and is issued by the Central Bank of Russia. The ruble is one of the world's oldest national currencies, with origins traced to the 13th century.

triples.name: Romanian leu
triples.description: The Romanian leu (symbol: L; currency code: RON) is the official currency of Romania. It is divided into 100 bani (singular: ban) and is issued by the National Bank of Romania. The word 'leu' is Romanian for 'lion'. The current leu was introduced in 2005 to replace the old leu at a ratio of 10,000 to 1.

triples.name: Peruvian sol
triples.description: The Peruvian sol (symbol: S/; currency code: PEN) is the official currency of Peru. It is divided into 100 céntimos and is issued by the Central Reserve Bank of Peru. The current sol replaced the nuevo sol in 2015, though it has the same value.

triples.name: Bahraini dinar
triples.description: The Bahraini dinar (symbol: .د.ب; currency code: BHD) is the official currency of Bahrain. It is divided into 1,000 fils and is issued by the Central Bank of Bahrain. The dinar has been pegged to the US dollar since 2001 at a rate of approximately 0.376 BHD per USD.

triples.name: Bulgarian lev
triples.description: The Bulgarian lev (currency code: BGN) is the official currency of Bulgaria. It is divided into 100 stotinki and is issued by the Bulgarian National Bank. The lev has been pegged to the euro since 1999 as part of a currency board arrangement.

triples.name: UAE dirham
triples.description: The United Arab Emirates dirham (symbol: د.إ; currency code: AED) is the official currency of the United Arab Emirates. It is divided into 100 fils and is issued by the Central Bank of the United Arab Emirates. It has been pegged to the US dollar since 1997.

triples.name: Israeli new shekel
triples.description: The Israeli new shekel (symbol: ₪; currency code: ILS) is the official currency of Israel and is also used in the Palestinian territories. It is divided into 100 agorot (singular: agora) and is issued by the Bank of Israel. It replaced the old shekel in 1985.

triples.name: Pound (sterling)
triples.description: Pound sterling (symbol: £; currency code: GBP) is the official currency of the United Kingdom and several British overseas territories and Crown Dependencies. It is the oldest currency still in continuous use and the fourth most-traded currency on the foreign exchange market. One pound is divided into 100 pence.

triples.name: ¥ / 円
triples.description: The yen sign (¥) and the Japanese kanji 円, both used as symbols for the Japanese yen.

triples.name: ¥ / 元
triples.description: The yuan sign (¥) and the Chinese character 元, both used as symbols for the renminbi.

triples.name: ₩ / 원
triples.description: The won sign (₩) and the Korean hangul 원, both used as symbols for the South Korean won.

triples.name: ISO 4217 code
triples.description: ISO 4217 is the international standard published by the International Organization for Standardization that defines three-letter alphabetic and three-digit numeric codes for the representation of currencies. For example, USD identifies the United States dollar and EUR identifies the euro.

triples.name: Symbol or abbreviation
triples.description: A symbol or abbreviation used to represent a currency in writing, such as $ for the US dollar, € for the euro, or £ for pound sterling. Currency symbols are typographic shorthand and are not standardised internationally (unlike ISO 4217 codes).

triples.name: Proportion of daily volume April 2019
triples.description: The share of total foreign exchange daily turnover attributable to a given currency in April 2019, as reported in the BIS Triennial Central Bank Survey. Because each transaction involves two currencies, the proportions across all currencies sum to 200 percent.

triples.name: Proportion of daily volume April 2022
triples.description: The share of total foreign exchange daily turnover attributable to a given currency in April 2022, as reported in the BIS Triennial Central Bank Survey. Because each transaction involves two currencies, the proportions across all currencies sum to 200 percent.

triples.name: yearly growth rate
triples.description: The percentage growth from one year to the next

triples.name: average turnover
triples.description: Turnover figures are often reported as averages (typically arithmetic means) over a defined period to give a representative value rather than a one-off snapshot.

triples.name: daily average turnover
triples.description: Daily average turnover expresses turnover as a per-day mean, calculated by dividing total turnover in a period by the number of trading days.

triples.name: in USD
triples.description: Indicates that a monetary value is expressed in United States dollars, the standard reporting unit for international foreign exchange statistics.

triples.name: net-net basis
triples.description: A reporting convention used in BIS foreign exchange surveys in which transactions are adjusted to remove double-counting both between local reporting dealers and between cross-border reporting dealers, yielding a true measure of global activity.

formulas.name: USD cross rate
formulas.expression: "cross rate" = "exchange rate" ( "source currency" , "US dollar" ) / "exchange rate" ( "target currency" , "US dollar" )
formulas.description: A cross rate is an exchange rate between two currencies, neither of which is the official currency of the country in which the quote is given. More generally, it is a rate derived from each currency's rate against a common third currency such as the US dollar.
